edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Θεὸς οὖν κατὰ τὴν χρηστότητα αὐτοῦ οὐ τοπικῶς ἀλλὰ προνοητικῶς συγκαταβαίνει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις. καὶ ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς οὐ τότε μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀεὶ μετὰ τῶν ἰδίων μαθητῶν ἐστι, πληρῶν τὸ „ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ᾿ ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.“ καὶ εἴπερ „κλῆμα καρπὸν οὐ δύναται φέρειν,“ „ἐὰν μὴ ἐμμείνῃ τῇ ἀμπέλῳ,“ δῆλον ὅτι καὶ οἱ τοῦ λόγου μαθηταὶ, τὰ νοητὰ τῆς ἀληθινῆς ἀμπέλου τοῦ λόγου „κλήματα,“ οὐ δύνανται φέρειν τοὺς καρποὺς τῆς ἀρετῆς, ἐὰν μὴ μένωσιν ἐν τῇ ἀληθινῇ ἀμπέλῳ, τῷ Χριστῷ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν τῶν τοπικῶς κάτω ἐπὶ γῆς τυγχάνοντι, ὃς μετὰ τῶν πανταχοῦ προσπεφυκότων αὐτῷ ὢν, ἤδη δὲ καὶ μετὰ τῶν οὐκ εἰδότων αὐτὸν πανταχοῦ ἐστι. καὶ τοῦτό γε ὁ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον γράψας Ἰωάννης ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ Ἰωάννου δηλοῖ, λέγοντος· „μέσος ὑμῶν στήκει, ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε, ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος.“ ἄτοπον δ᾿ ἐστὶν, τοῦ πληρώσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ εἰπόντος· „οὐχὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐγὼ πληρῶ; λέγει κύριος“ ὄντος μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν καὶ πλησίον ἡμῶν τυγχάνοντος (πιστεύω γὰρ αὐτῷ λέγοντι· „θεὸς ἐγγίζων ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ οὐ θεὸς πόῤῥωθεν. λέγει κύριος“), ζητεῖν εὔχεσθαι τῷ μὴ φθάνοντι ἐπὶ τὰ σύμπαντα ἡλίῳ ἢ σελήνῃ ἤ τινι τῶν ἀστέρων. ἔστω δὲ, ἵνα αὐταῖς ταῖς λέξεσι Κέλσου χρήσωμαι, προφητεύοντας εἶναι ὑετοὺς καὶ θάλπη καὶ νέφη καὶ βροντὰς ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην καὶ ἀστέρας· ἆρ᾿ οὖν, εἰ προφητεύουσιν οὗτοι τὰ τηλικαῦτα, οὐχὶ μᾶλλον τῷ θεῷ, ᾧ ὑπουργοῦντες προφητεύουσι, προσκυνητέον κἀκεῖνον σεπτέον ἤπερ τοῖς προφήταις αὐτοῦ; προφητευέτωσαν οὖν καὶ ἀστραπὰς καὶ καρποὺς καὶ γονὰς ἁπάσας, καὶ πάντα ταμιευέσθωσαν τὰ τοιαῦτα· ἀλλ᾿ οὐ διὰ τοῦτο προσκυνήσομεν τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ὡς οὐδὲ Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς μετ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐκ θεοῦ προφητεύσαντας τὰ κρείττονα ὑετῶν τε καὶ θάλπους καὶ νεφῶν καὶ βροντῶν καὶ ἀστραπῶν καὶ καρπῶν καὶ πασῶν γονῶν αἰσθητῶν. ἀλλὰ κἂν ἔχωσιν ἥλιος καὶ σελήνη καὶ ἀστέρες προφητεύειν προφητείας κρείττονας ὑετῶν, οὐδ᾿ οὕτως αὐτοὺς ἀλλὰ τὸν πατέρα τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς προφητειῶν καὶ τὸν διάκονον αὐτῶν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ προσκυνήσομεν. ἀλλ᾿ ἔστω καὶ κήρυκας αὐτοῦ εἶναι καὶ ἀληθῶς οὐρανίους ἀγγέλους, πῶς οὖν οὐχὶ καὶ οὕτως τὸν κηρυσσόμενον ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν θεὸν καὶ τὸν ἀγγελλόμενον μᾶλλον προσκυνητέον ἢ τοὺς κήρυκας καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ;
thought_title: God is near; the stars are only his heralds
pass_a_gloss: God then, according to his kindness (χρηστότητα), not locally (τοπικῶς) but providentially (προνοητικῶς) comes down with (συγκαταβαίνει) men. And the Child (παῖς) of God not then only but always is with his own disciples, fulfilling (πληρῶν) 'behold I am with you all the days until the completion (συντελείας) of the age.' And if 'a branch (κλῆμα) cannot bear fruit unless it remain in the vine (ἀμπέλῳ)', it is clear that the disciples of the Word too, the intelligible (νοητά) 'branches' of the true vine of the Word, cannot bear the fruits of virtue (ἀρετῆς) unless they remain in the true vine, the Christ of God, who is also with us who are locally below on earth; who, being with those everywhere grown onto (προσπεφυκότων) him, and indeed with those not knowing him, is everywhere. And this John who wrote the gospel shows from the person (προσώπου) of John the Baptist, saying: 'In the midst of you stands one whom you do not know, coming after me.' It is absurd (ἄτοπον), when he who filled heaven and earth and said 'Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord' is with us and near us (for I believe him saying: 'I am a God drawing near (ἐγγίζων), and not a God from afar, says the Lord'), to seek to pray to the sun not reaching (φθάνοντι) to all things, or moon, or one of the stars. Let it be, to use Celsus's very words (λέξεσι), that sun, moon and stars are prophesying (προφητεύοντας) rains, heats (θάλπη), clouds and thunders; then if these prophesy such great things, must one not rather worship God, whom serving (ὑπουργοῦντες) they prophesy, and revere (σεπτέον) him than his prophets? Let them prophesy also lightnings and fruits and all generations (γονάς), and let them dispense (ταμιευέσθωσαν) all such things; but not on this account will we worship those who worship, as neither Moses and those after him who prophesied from God things better than rains, heat, clouds, thunders, lightnings, fruits and all perceptible generations. But even if sun, moon and stars are able to prophesy prophecies better than rains, not even so will we worship them but the Father of the prophecies in them and his minister (διάκονον) the Word of God. But let them be also his heralds (κήρυκας) and truly heavenly angels (ἀγγέλους); how then even so must one not rather worship the God heralded (κηρυσσόμενον) by them and announced (ἀγγελλόμενον) than his heralds and angels?

pass_b_english: God, then, in his kindness comes down to men, not in a spatial sense but by his providence. And the Child of God is with his own disciples not only at that time but always, fulfilling the words, “Behold, I am with you all the days, until the end of the age” (Matthew 28:20). And if “a branch cannot bear fruit unless it abides in the vine” (John 15:4), it is clear that the disciples of the Word as well, the spiritual “branches” (John 15:5) of the true vine, the Word (John 15:1), cannot bear the fruits of virtue unless they remain in the true vine, the Christ of God. He is with us too, whose place is here below on earth; and being with those everywhere who have grown into him, and indeed with those who do not know him, he is everywhere. John, who wrote the Gospel, shows this too in the person of John the Baptist, who says: “Among you stands one whom you do not know, who comes after me” (John 1:26–27).

Since he who has filled heaven and earth, and has said, “Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord” (Jeremiah 23:24), is with us and is near us (for I believe him when he says, “I am a God at hand, and not a God far off, says the Lord” (Jeremiah 23:23)), it is absurd to seek to pray to the sun or the moon or any of the stars, which do not reach to all things.

But let it be granted, to use Celsus’s very words, that the sun, the moon and the stars are “prophesying rains and heat and clouds and thunder”. If, then, they prophesy such great things, should we not rather worship God, in whose service they prophesy, and revere him rather than his prophets? Let them, then, prophesy “lightnings, too, and fruits and every kind of offspring”, and let them “dispense” all such things; yet we will not for that reason worship those who themselves worship, just as we do not worship Moses either, or those after him who prophesied from God things better than rain and heat and clouds and thunder and lightning and fruits and every offspring the senses perceive. But even if the sun, the moon and the stars were able to utter prophecies better than rains, not even so will we worship them, but the Father of the prophecies in them, and the Word of God, who is the minister of those prophecies.
But grant that they are also his “heralds” and “truly heavenly angels”. Even so, how should we not worship the God whom they herald and announce, rather than his heralds and his angels?
notes: ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς rendered 'the Child of God' (the title of Acts 4:27, 30; possible allusion, left uncited). 'Not only at that time' = during his earthly life. The marked phrases 'prophesying rains and heat and clouds and thunder', 'lightnings, too, and fruits and every kind of offspring', 'dispense', 'heralds' and 'truly heavenly angels' are Celsus's own words from his passage quoted in 5.6. ἀγγέλους / ἀγγελλόμενον is a wordplay (angels / announced) that English cannot keep fully. Jeremiah 23:23 LXX is a statement ('I am a God at hand'), whereas the Hebrew is a question; LXX and English verse numbers agree in Jeremiah 23. The closing clause (τὸν διάκονον αὐτῶν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ) is rendered 'the Word of God, who serves him in them'; literally 'their minister, the Word of God'. The 'true vine' (John 15:1) and 'branches' (John 15:5) are cited as allusions. νοητά ('intelligible', grasped by the mind) is rendered 'spiritual' for readability; it is not πνευματικός.

Open doubt (review): 5.12: νοητὰ κλήματα is rendered 'spiritual branches' so it reads well. The Greek word means 'grasped by the mind' and is not πνευματικός. This is recorded in translator_notes and needs no owner call.
